activities.label: verify finite-pupil image formation and retinal inversion

queries.question: Does a reduced eye/camera model trace a full screen image through a finite pupil and equivalent lens onto an inverted retinal plane before binocular disparity is introduced?

assumptions: The cornea and crystalline lens are represented by one equivalent paraxial thin lens.
The pupil is circular and the retina is a plane in the first reduced model.
The screen is a luminous planar source and each source point emits a finite ray bundle toward the pupil.
The retinal image is an optical projection; the brain-side interpretation is not simulated.
kill_tests: A focused normal model must collapse a finite pupil ray bundle to one retinal point.
A positive screen height must map to a negative retinal height.
Increasing pupil radius must increase the blur of an out-of-focus model.
Astigmatism must expose two meridional image distances; it must not be represented as one point focus.
unknowns: How well this reduced model predicts a particular person's retinal image.
How curved-retina and cornea/lens surfaces change peripheral projection.
How a future binocular display should constrain disparity without causing discomfort.
